guide: Open Start and set your agency name and targets in the yellow cells. A one-person agency can use the Schedule, Open Shifts and Fill Rate pages without the matching tables.

Replace the demo data. Fill Caregivers (a caregiver is also called a carer, care worker or support worker), Clients, Availability and Time Off, then the Schedule (also called a rota or roster) with one row per visit.
Check Weekly Grid by Caregiver every Friday: hours above the overtime line (overtime means hours above the weekly line), the own weekly limit, days in a row and short rests turn red or amber.

Open Shifts lists visits without a caregiver. Match Scores ranks the candidates for each shift with the weights you set in Match Weights, and shows the cost of regular hours, overtime and the cover premium.

Log every call-off (a caregiver cannot come) on Call-offs and Cover with the reason, notice and the minutes to find cover. Cover means another caregiver takes the visit. Cover Cost by Month shows the cost per call-off.
Use Continuity by Client and Weekly Grid by Client to see how few different caregivers each client sees. Fill Rate by Week shows planned, cover and uncovered hours against your target.
Use the 18 decision tools: each ends with a verdict and a what-if table. Print 12 sheets and 12 documents, follow 12 checklists and send 34 ready messages.
Holidays holds the pay and bill multipliers (a holiday is a bank holiday or public holiday). Plan extra caregivers with the Holiday Cover Planner and the Holiday Cover Sheet.
Why a workbook: flat price, no per-client or per-caregiver fee, no rise when hours grow, your data stays with you. It takes typed or pasted times; no live app, no GPS.
Read the Schedule KPI Dashboard and Charts every week: fill rate, open shifts, overtime, call-offs, cover cost and continuity. Check your own local rules and confirm pay questions with your adviser.

listing.title: Home Care Agency Schedule Excel Template: Open Shifts, Caregiver Matching, Call-offs and Cover, Overtime Check, Fill Rate
listing.headline: Fill open shifts faster and keep overtime and call-offs under control
listing.description:
Run the weekly schedule of a small home care agency in one Excel workbook. Built for an owner-director with a scheduler and care coordinator, field supervisors and about 40 caregivers: non-medical care, hours, dates and rates only.

Weekly Grid by Caregiver shows every caregiver's hours against the overtime line and the own weekly limit, the days in a row and rest between visits. Open Shifts lists visits without a caregiver with their urgency, and Match Scores ranks the candidates for each shift with weights you set (skills, area, language, availability, client preference and hours booked) and the cost of regular hours, overtime and the short-notice cover premium. Continuity by Client counts the different caregivers each client sees. Call-offs and Cover records the reason, notice, minutes to find cover and the premium paid, and Cover Cost by Month and Fill Rate by Week show cost per call-off and the share of hours covered against your target.

18 decision tools answer weekly questions with a verdict and a what-if table: weekly schedule checker, open shift filler with the three best caregivers, cover option cost, matching score, continuity index, call-off response plan, call-off rate check, cover cost against history, fill rate forecast, rest and days-off checks, posting deadline, hours balance, standby pool sizing, free hours finder, holiday cover planner and call-off sensitivity. Print 12 sheets and 12 documents, follow 12 checklists and send 34 ready text messages.

This is part two of the Home Care Agency suite. A standard .xlsx workbook with no macros and no subscription, one flat price with no per-client or per-caregiver fee, your data stays with you, 15 languages in one purchase, with a demo copy full of sample data. It takes times typed or pasted from whatever you use; it has no live app and no GPS, and it does not promise any outcome.
